Bloom Energy stock is taking a hit today.
Bloom Energy Stock Slides as AI Trade Unwinds
Anthropic PBC.’s
record-setting IPO was
to reassure investors about AI. The company sold shares at $83 on Nov. 19, topping its $70-to-$78 target range, and raised $81.3 billion, an IPO record.

Since then, investors sitting on AI gains have been banking them, and the pullback has hit data center infrastructure stocks such as Bloom Energy, whose outlook rides on how much AI infrastructure gets funded down the road.
Scrutiny of Anthropic’s own results is feeding the selling. Seaport Global analyst
Jay Goldberg
pointed to growth that fell 101 percentage points, from 144% in the second quarter to 43% in the third.
Goldberg estimates Anthropic needs strong quarterly gains, in the high double digits, for two straight years to back up its valuation.

A heavy bill sits behind Anthropic’s plan to construct and run data-center capacity it would own. Goldberg calls it a major execution risk and puts the cash flow required for all commitments near $900 billion, with about $640 billion due by 2030.

Any stumble there matters to Bloom Energy. If growth cools or funding gets harder to find at Anthropic, data center buildouts could slow, and that could hurt data center infrastructure firms such as Bloom Energy.
Dan Ives
of Yorkville Ives & Co
the deal is additionally siphoning some liquidity from other tech names, so there is less cash for stocks like Bloom Energy.
Debt, Borrowing Costs and Trump Add to the Strain
Over the last ten years, big tech mostly paid for data centers out of operating cash. That model is breaking down this year.
During the three months through September, Alphabet’s spending
$9.1 billion past its operating cash, and Meta’s ran $2.1 billion past. Amazon’s cash burn, measured by free cash flow, reached $42.4 billion over the past year.

For Bloom Energy, the risk is that these borrowers are the ones funding data center construction. If financing gets pricier or bond investors pull back, expansion could slow, which might cut demand for the infrastructure that data centers need.
Policy adds a layer of uncertainty abroad. President
Donald Trump
is backing the American Affordability and Jobs Act in the Senate, and he says the bill would speed energy projects and make data centers cover their power costs.
He also warned that China may draw the data center investment the U.S. turns down.

A Monday Commerce Department rule now demands export licenses for top-end AI chips headed to Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil, countries Washington says carry higher-than-normal diversion risk.
A slowdown in AI infrastructure spending, or tougher limits on buildouts abroad, could hurt data center infrastructure stocks, Bloom Energy among them.
BE Shares Are Tanking
BE Price Action:
Bloom Energy shares were down 14.44% at $143.84 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro.
